stops.title: A Great Light
stops.summary: Centuries before Bethlehem, Isaiah promises a child who will carry the government on His shoulders.
stops.why: Isaiah wrote this to people living in real darkness: war, fear, a failing nation. God's answer was a baby. Christmas didn't come out of nowhere. It was a promise kept, and the names Isaiah gave tell you who that child is.

quiz.q: Which is NOT one of the names Isaiah gives the child?
What did the people walking in darkness see?
Whose throne will the child reign on?

stops.title: Be It Unto Me
stops.summary: The angel Gabriel tells a young woman in Nazareth that she will carry the Son of God.
stops.why: Mary was young, engaged and about to have a story no one would believe. Saying yes could cost her marriage, her reputation and possibly her life. She asked an honest question, then said yes anyway. Faith isn't the absence of questions.

card.name: Mary
card.title: The Willing Servant
card.strength: Said yes to God at great personal risk.
card.weakness: Scripture records her questions, not failures: "How shall this be?"

quiz.q: What town was Mary living in?
"Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it unto me according to thy word."

stops.title: The Quiet Yes
stops.summary: Joseph plans to quietly call off the marriage, until an angel speaks to him in a dream.
stops.why: Joseph never says a word in the Bible, but his actions say everything. He planned to protect Mary from public shame even when he thought she'd betrayed him. When God spoke, he obeyed right away and raised a son who wasn't his. Strength can be quiet.

card.name: Joseph
card.title: The Quiet Protector
card.strength: Obeyed at once and protected his family.
card.weakness: Planned to quietly divorce Mary before the angel spoke.

quiz.q: How did the angel speak to Joseph?
Why was the baby to be named Jesus?
options: He would save His people from their sins

stops.title: Born in Bethlehem
stops.summary: No room in the inn, a manger for a bed, and angels announcing it to shepherds.
stops.why: The King of the universe was born in a feeding trough, and the announcement went first to shepherds, who were rough, working men on the night shift. God's biggest news went to the people the world overlooked.

quiz.q: Whose decree sent Joseph and Mary to Bethlehem?
Who heard the news first from the angels?

stops.title: Following the Star
stops.summary: Wise men travel from the east, follow a star and bring gifts to the young King.
stops.why: Foreigners crossed a long distance to worship a child, while the king in Jerusalem felt threatened by Him. Jesus divides people even now: some come looking for Him, some see Him as a threat. Then the wise men went home another way.

quiz.q: Which was NOT one of the wise men's gifts?
Which king was troubled by the news?
Why did the wise men go home another way?
options: God warned them in a dream
